title: Finite-Tor realization of the structure-morphism Hom chain
statement:
Use the Poincare conventions [def-pod-conventions], with $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ the admissible structure morphism, $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Use finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], ordinary and exceptional adjunctions [fix-prop-adjunctions], restricted tensor–Hom adjunction [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions], projection [def-exchange-projection, fix-prop-projection-formula], and currying conventions [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. For $N,T\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ put
$$C=Ra_!K,\qquad L_N=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Ra^!N),\qquad A_N=Ra_*L_N,\qquad B_N=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,N).$$
Then $C,A_N,B_N$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, and $Ra^!N,L_N,La^*T,K\otimes^LLa^*T$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. This includes $N=\Lambda_s$ and $N=\omega_{s,\Lambda}=R(\operatorname{id}_s)^!\Lambda_s$; the coefficient unit has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$.
Write $\varepsilon_{L_N}:La^*A_N\to L_N$, $\mu_N:Ra_!Ra^!N\to N$, and $P_T:C\otimes^LT\to Ra_!(K\otimes^LLa^*T)$ for the chosen counits and projection. Define
$$p_N=\mu_N\circ Ra_!\bigl(\operatorname{ev}_{K,Ra^!N}\circ(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_{L_N})\bigr)\circ P_{A_N},\qquad \alpha_N=\operatorname{curry}(p_N):A_N\to B_N.$$
Both specified canonical isomorphisms [lem-sf-tensor-hom] and [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction] at $(a,K,N)$ have underlying morphism $\alpha_N$. Their reverse Hom chain, from $\operatorname{Hom}_s(T,A_N)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_s(T,B_N)$, is postcomposition with $\alpha_N$ for every finite-Tor test object $T$. For every $b:N\to N'$ one has
$$\alpha_{N'}\circ Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Ra^!b)=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,b)\circ\alpha_N.$$
All assertions use completed operations at $\mathcal O_E$, raw scalar localization at $E$, and a common finite coefficient-field stage at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. No site-perfectness of $K$ or properness of $a$ is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-hom-chain-ctf-domains] with $f=a$, $M=K$, $Y=s$. The Poincare hypotheses make $a$ a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes with the required exceptional adjunction. Its seven membership assertions give exactly $C,A_N,B_N,Ra^!N,L_N,La^*T,K\otimes^LLa^*T$ in the stated finite-Tor categories. In particular $P_{A_N}$ and all five Hom bijections are defined at each coefficient stage.

source.place: Steps 1–2: the five Hom bijections and their canonical representing map

proof.text: The coefficient-object theorem [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible] puts $\Lambda_s$ in the bounded constructible point category. At finite coefficients $\Lambda_s\otimes^L M=M$ for every degree-zero module sheaf $M$, so its Tor amplitude is $[0,0]$. Integrally each reduction is the finite unit by that theorem, so the same interval works for every reduction; at field stages use the defining equality $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Thus $N=\Lambda_s$ is allowed. By [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], $\omega_{s,\Lambda}\cong\Lambda_s$, so it is allowed too.

source.place: Steps 1–2: the five Hom bijections and their canonical representing map

proof.text: For $t:T\to A_N$, specialize [lem-pod-hom-chain-counit-formula] to $(a,K,N)$. Its $p_N$ is literally the displayed $p_N$: the ordinary counit, evaluation, exceptional counit and chosen projection occur in the same order. Hence its composite $\Phi_T^N$ is postcomposition with $\alpha_N=\operatorname{curry}(p_N)$ for every finite-Tor $T$. In particular $\Phi_{A_N}^N(1_{A_N})=\alpha_N$.

source.place: Steps 1–2: the five Hom bijections and their canonical representing map

proof.text: Here is the representing-map identification for the specified canonical isomorphisms [lem-sf-tensor-hom, fix-lem-tensor-adjunction]. In both constructions the forward Hom chain $h_T$ runs from $\operatorname{Hom}(T,B_N)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(T,A_N)$: uncurry, precompose with $P_T^{-1}$, exceptional adjunction, curry, ordinary adjunction. Reversing these five specified bijections gives precisely $\Phi_T^N$ of step 3; in particular the projection arrow reverses to precomposition with $P_T$, not $P_T^{-1}$. The chosen canonical representing arrow is therefore $h_{A_N}^{-1}(1_{A_N})=\Phi_{A_N}^N(1_{A_N})=\alpha_N$ in each construction. Explicitly set $r=h_{B_N}(1_{B_N})$. Naturality in $T$ gives $h_T(u)=r\circ u$ and $(h_T)^{-1}(v)=\alpha_N\circ v$. The inverse-bijection identities at the two identity arrows yield $r\circ\alpha_N=1_{A_N}$ and $\alpha_N\circ r=1_{B_N}$. Thus the representing arrow is an isomorphism, with exactly the required direction. This is the identity-component calculation defining the canonical comparison, not an identification based merely on existence of an abstract isomorphism.

source.place: Steps 1–2: the five Hom bijections and their canonical representing map

proof.text: For $b:N\to N'$ put $u=Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Ra^!b)$ and $v=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,b)$. Naturality in $N$ of [lem-pod-hom-chain-counit-formula] gives $\Phi_{A_N}^{N'}(u)=v\circ\Phi_{A_N}^{N}(1_{A_N})$. Step 3 identifies the left side with $\alpha_{N'}\circ u$ and the right side with $v\circ\alpha_N$, the claimed equality. The domain and counit-formula lemmas expressly use completed integral operations, rationalization and common finite stages, so every preceding equality is an equality in the chosen coefficient category. The argument never invokes the coefficient-dual tensor formula for $K$ or the proper identification $Ra_!=Ra_*$.
